title: The wobble period of 110 of 261 tested Gaia FPR binary-asteroid candidate windows is the rotation period or half of it, so these wobbles are mainly rotation photocentre signals
abstract: Question: Liberato et al. (2026) list 343 binary-asteroid candidates (410 windows) from periodic along-scan residuals in the Gaia Focused Product Release (FPR). Is the wobble period the rotation period of the asteroid, which a single turning body gives through its light centre? Method: We compared each wobble period with the Asteroid Lightcurve Database (LCDB, U >= 2-) rotation period P_rot. We counted matches at P_rot/2, P_rot and 2 P_rot (5 % tolerance) against two permutation nulls. We repeated the test in all 11,943 windows of the published FPR period search that have an LCDB period. We modelled the light centre of a rotating ellipsoid with Horizons phase angles and the Gaia scan angle. Results: Of 261 candidate windows (207 objects), 73 match P_rot (11.7 expected) and 37 match P_rot/2 (7.5 expected); 2 P_rot has no excess (9 vs 13.5). Of the 183 windows with P_rot inside the 7-h search limit, 60 % match (21 expected). Five objects change between P_rot and P_rot/2 from one window to the next, which an orbit cannot do. The two DR3 candidates with repeated periods and two occultation-flagged objects also match rotation. In the parent search, 34 % of the strongest signals (p < 0.1 %) match, against 5 % expected. The rotation share rises with apparent size: 17 % below 12 mas and 44-48 % above. Matched amplitudes scale with apparent size and agree with a limb-darkened (Lambert) ellipsoid within a factor of about 2; a Lommel-Seeliger ellipsoid is about 25 times too small. Conclusion: At least 110 tested windows are rotation photocentre signals, not satellites, unless the orbit is synchronous; about 28 % of all 410 windows by extrapolation. Limitations: Only 64 % of windows have LCDB periods; a direct match misses P_rot < 7 h, higher harmonics and true-sampling aliases, so this is a lower limit; the model is a smooth ellipsoid; the 151 unmatched windows stay undecided.
